gap: No result ChatGPT got states which hardwire kit each maker names for its under-$200 3-channel camera and what it costs: on 2026-11-21 that puts the Vantrue N4S ($199.99) over $200 with any Vantrue kit, keeps the Redtiger F17 at $165.98 with Redtiger's kit, and leaves the Rexing C3 needing a dedicated GPS logger and a kit Rexing does not name.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages I could open (vortexradar.com returned HTTP 403, so it was not read). productbible.com names one hardwire kit, the HK6-F for the VIOFO T330, and the $149.99 Vantrue LTE module; it gives no kit or kit price for the N4S. dattatecblog.com says only 'Budget an extra $15 to $25 for the kit', names no kit for the F17 and no microSD limit for any model. us.my-best.com mentions no hardwire kits at all, and none of its eight models is an under-$200 pick from the chats except the older Vantrue N4. None of them states the Rexing C3's GPS logger restriction or that the F17's 4K front mode is described with the inside camera off. ChatGPT's own answer only warned generically that a kit and card 'can push the total above $200'.
decides: For a shopper who wants parking mode inside $200, the N4S drops out: $199.99 plus the cheapest kit whose listing names it ($29.99) is $229.98. The Redtiger F17 with its kit ($165.98) and the older Vantrue OnDash N4 with a kit ($129.98) stay under. For driving-only use the N4S still fits the budget by one cent. The Rexing C3 is the weakest fit on compatibility: GPS is a separate dedicated logger and no Rexing kit listing I read names the C3. One caveat on method: Vantrue, Redtiger, Rexing and DDPAI product pages returned HTTP 429 today, so every maker figure below was read from the store's own search record for that product (listing text and price), not the rendered page.
